title: Accenture Acquires Sagacity Solutions to Scale AI-Driven Customer Intelligence Across Accenture Song’s UK & Ireland Operations
snippet: LONDON; Oct. 13, 2026 – Accenture (NYSE: ACN) has acquired Sagacity, a UK-based data and customer intelligence firm, strengthening Accenture Song’s capacity to deliver AI-powered customer reinvention at scale. The acquisition directly addresses growing client demand to connect data, AI and operations infrastructure into unified, outcome-focused programmes that drive measurable business results.
fullText:
Founded in 2005 by Anita Dougall, Malka Townshend and Harry Dougall, and headquartered in London, Sagacity brings differentiated data assets, AI-enabled technology and deep customer intelligence expertise. Combined with Accenture's industry, technology and customer operations capabilities, these strengths will help organisations turn customer insight into more personalised, proactive experiences at scale, from strategy and design through implementation and operations.

        

          

            
            
            
            
          

        

        

This move reflects Accenture's strategy of using acquisitions to scale in high-growth areas and deepen industry-specific capabilities - in this case bringing together customer intelligence, AI and operational expertise at a scale that directly addresses how clients in industries with large customer bases and complex customer journeys, such as utilities, retail, banking and telecommunications, are looking to secure revenues and grow.

        

The addition of more than 140 professionals expands Accenture Song's UK and Ireland delivery capability across strategy, design, implementation and operations, enabling clients to move from customer insight to intelligent action faster and at greater scale than either organisation could achieve independently.

        

"Our clients are increasingly looking to connect data, AI and operations to drive growth and reinvent customer experiences," said Sohel Aziz, senior managing director, Accenture Song, UK and Ireland. "Sagacity’s deep expertise and outcome-focused approach will enhance our ability to help clients turn insight into action and achieve measurable results through intelligent customer operations. Together, we can help organisations move faster, make smarter decisions and create sustainable value."

        

"Joining Accenture represents an exciting opportunity to accelerate the impact of our people, data and technology," said Anita Dougall, CEO and co-founder of Sagacity. "By combining our expertise, data and know-how with Accenture's scale and innovation capabilities, we can help more organisations deliver meaningful business results."

        

Terms of the transaction were not disclosed.

title: Reinvented with Accenture
snippet: The new brand campaign, “Let there be change,” will triple the company’s annual media spend to $90 million. Developed with acclaimed creative agency Droga5, part of Accenture Interactive, the campaign depicts...
fullText:
The new brand campaign, “Let there be change,” will triple the company’s annual media spend to $90 million. Developed with acclaimed creative agency Droga5, part of Accenture Interactive, the campaign depicts change — both seismic and small — optimistically capturing its power and beauty and reflecting the depth and breadth of Accenture’s expertise.

        

“Exponential changes in technology were transforming the way we work and live before COVID-19, and now its impact has raised change to a new level, requiring companies to reimagine everything and requiring economies and entire industries to rebuild,” said Julie Sweet, chief executive officer, Accenture. “In this moment, to emerge stronger there is only one choice: embrace change and ensure that it benefits all — your customers, people, shareholders, partners and communities.”

        

To create this shared success, the company is pioneering “360° Value”— helping clients transform and reinvent their businesses, reskill their employees, or become more sustainable. This builds on Accenture’s successful rotation to “the New,” with approximately 70 percent of its business now in digital, cloud and security, which is critical at a time when scale matters to help its clients transform their entire enterprises.

New Purpose and Brand

Accenture’s purpose — to deliver on the promise of technology and human ingenuity — will guide the company’s strategy, priorities, and the opportunities it creates for its more than 500,000 people. Accenture reflects the human ingenuity of Accenture’s talented people and their commitment to using technology to deliver value for all its stakeholders.

Accenture’s purpose and brand are grounded in its enduring formula for market leadership: embracing change and continually transforming its business to create value, powered by the talent and creativity of its people. Last year, Accenture invested nearly $900 million in training and development, $1.5 billion in acquisitions, and approximately $900 million in research and development. Accenture also recently announced the creation of Accenture Cloud First, a new multi-service group of 70,000 cloud professionals, with a $3 billion investment over three years.

        

“We are following the same advice we give our clients in this time of relentless change: act with great agility and boldness,” said Amy Fuller, chief marketing and communications officer, Accenture. “Our new campaign captures our purpose and gives voice to a mission-critical issue: How can we help our clients embrace change to better businesses, communities, and lives?”

The brand campaign launches simultaneously across all of Accenture’s internal and external digital properties, through television and online advertising, including social media campaigns across the Americas, Europe and Asia. The new creative leverages the Accenture symbol — “>” — which has been part of the company’s logo for more than 20 years, and will affect every touch point.

“From a creative perspective, this was a massively exciting brief and opportunity,” said David Droga, founder and creative chairman, Droga5. “More than just creating a new purpose and campaign, we worked closely with leadership teams, people and clients around the world at every step to help shape the future of our company. This marks a bold evolution for all of us at Accenture.”

Acquired by Accenture Interactive in 2019, Droga5 is a globally acclaimed creative agency that has become synonymous with high-caliber, influential and industry-defining work. Recently named agency of the decade by both Advertising Age and Adweek, Droga5 fulfills Accenture Interactive’s ambition of building a new agency model that delivers seamless, rewarding brand experiences to clients and consumers at every touchpoint.

Accenture is currently ranked number 31 on Interbrand’s ranking of the top 100 global brands, with a brand value of over $16.2 billion. That represents more than a 212% increase in value since 2002, when the company debuted at number 53 on the Interbrand ranking.

About Accenture

Accenture is a global professional services company with leading capabilities in digital, cloud and security. Combining unmatched experience and specialized skills across more than 40 industries, we offer Strategy and Consulting, Interactive, Technology and Operations services—all powered by the world’s largest network of Advanced Technology and Intelligent Operations centers. Our 506,000 people deliver on the promise of technology and human ingenuity every day, serving clients in more than 120 countries. We embrace the power of change to create value and shared success for our clients, people, shareholders, partners and communities. Visit us at www.accenture.com.

title: Accenture to Acquire Alfahealth, Expanding Digital Health Capabilities to Accelerate Healthcare Transformation in Italy
snippet: Alfahealth brings more than two decades of experience developing and operating technology capabilities, delivered as part of its services-plus-product model to support patient journeys, including clinical...
fullText:
Alfahealth brings more than two decades of experience developing and operating technology capabilities, delivered as part of its services-plus-product model to support patient journeys, including clinical workflows and diagnostics, as well as administrative and operational processes. Its technology enables providers to connect data and support new, more integrated models of care at the scale and regulatory rigor demanded by the Italian market.

        

          

            
            
            
            
          

        

        

The acquisition reflects Accenture’s continued strategy to combine services, software, data and AI-powered platforms, using an integrated services and product commercial model, so clients achieve sustainable end-to-end transformation. Alfahealth’s positioning in the industry will be further enhanced with Accenture’s capabilities in data, AI, cybersecurity and cloud.

        

“Italy is at a pivotal moment in the transformation of its healthcare system, with growing investments in digital health, interoperability and new models of care,” said Teodoro Lio, Market Unit Lead for Accenture in Italy. “Alfahealth brings deep healthcare expertise, trusted relationships with healthcare organizations across Italy and capabilities for digitizing and orchestrating the clinical and administrative processes of our healthcare ecosystem. Together, we will help healthcare providers and institutions accelerate innovation, improve care delivery and enable more connected, data-driven and personalized experiences for all Italians, powered by data and artificial intelligence.”

        

Alfahealth brings approximately 1,200 specialized professionals to Accenture Italy’s Health practice, and a strong position in the Italian healthcare sector, supporting relevant national programs in a regulated environment.

        

Terms of the transaction were not disclosed. Completion of the acquisition is subject to customary closing conditions.

title: Accenture and Dell Technologies Expand Collaboration to Help Enterprises Scale Private AI and Modernize Infrastructure
snippet: Accenture and Dell Technologies today announced a major expansion of their 20+ year collaboration with the formation of the Accenture Dell Business Group, designed to help organizations scale AI within their own environment and modernize their infrastructure. Together, the companies can give enterprises greater control over their data, more predictable economics, and the performance needed to run enterprise-grade agentic AI workloads.
fullText:
“By expanding our collaboration with Dell, we’re strengthening the power of our organizations to help our clients move from AI ambition to scaled execution to measurable business outcomes," said Julie Sweet, chair and CEO, Accenture. "Enterprises will be able to deploy AI solutions faster, align them with their business priorities, maintain greater control through private, hybrid and sovereign environments, and optimize both cost and performance."

        

          

            
            
            
            
          

        

        

“Dell Technologies and Accenture bring a deep history of working side-by-side to help our customers unlock their biggest opportunities,” said Michael Dell, chairman and CEO, Dell Technologies. “The formation of a dedicated business group deepens that collaboration to help enterprises move from AI interest to adoption. By bringing together Accenture’s strategic and industry expertise with Dell’s AI-ready infrastructure and services, we’re helping customers streamline business processes and build the full-stack capabilities needed to deploy AI at scale.”

        

The Accenture Dell Business Group builds on a strong track record of helping clients in industries such as financial services, life sciences, manufacturing, industrials and high-tech use AI to transform their businesses. It is uniquely positioned to help organizations deploy AI on private infrastructure, leveraging relationships with sovereign and neo cloud providers.

        

For RHAELM, a UK-based AI infrastructure and solutions provider, Accenture and Dell are contributing to accelerating the delivery of its sovereign cloud solutions, focused on secure, compliant, high-performing operations.

        

“By leveraging Dell’s AI-ready infrastructure and services and Accenture’s deep industry and transformation expertise, we are enabling our clients to deploy cutting-edge sovereign AI at pace and scale,” said Bradd Lewis, CEO and CRO, RHAELM. “The Accenture Dell Business Group brings a deeper level of collaboration that directly benefits our clients.”

        

To support the Accenture Dell Business Group, Accenture plans to train more than 3,000 practitioners to build deep capability and expertise across the Dell portfolio. This group will deliver comprehensive solutions to help organizations complement their cloud strategies with on-premises AI infrastructure — particularly for those in highly regulated industries. Together, these capabilities provide a unified approach to accelerating AI adoption while aligning technology investments to business outcomes:
